editorial_reason: The source independently states both the global two-variable Lipschitz condition and a point-anchored (one fixed argument) condition. Global Lipschitz implies the anchored bound for every point, but an anchored bound at one point does not imply a uniform two-point Lipschitz constant on any neighborhood. It should not be conflated with the common 'locally Lipschitz at a' convention requiring the two-point inequality on some neighborhood of a. ProofWiki also gives a real-interval specialization; here that is documented as a specialization, not counted as an additional independent context. No requirement that X be complete, compact or connected.

ProofWiki supplies two equivalent presentations of unrooted simple connected acyclic graphs: no circuits and no cycles. For undirected simple graphs, a circuit contains a cycle, making their absence equivalent, even without finiteness; they should share one mathematical meaning with two individually sourced formulations. The source separately mentions rooted tree as an alternative terminology, but the root, parent and child structures are not independently defined here; do not silently turn the unrooted meaning into a rooted tree. A tree can be finite or infinite; do not impose finite vertex set. The empty-graph connectedness convention is not settled by this source and must not be asserted.

Both source sections are independently visible and their quantifiers differ: binary independence is the event-product criterion for two sub-σ-algebras, whereas an indexed family requires factorization for all finite collections of DISTINCT indices. Mere pairwise independence does not imply mutual independence for three or more σ-algebras, so these are separate mathematical contexts rather than equivalent presentations of one fixed family property. The countable formulation does not require countable intersections of arbitrary events in the condition; only finite subsets are tested. All events must be measurable in the same ambient probability space. This source has an incidental inconsistent notation for the ambient σ-algebra in its binary paragraph, resolved by the explicit surrounding probability-space notation rather than quoted verbatim.

ProofWiki defines a sequence of random variables taking values in one measurable space as independent precisely when their generated σ-algebras are mutually independent. The generated σ-algebra is X_n^{-1}(S), i.e. the collection of preimages of all measurable subsets of S, not the single preimage of the whole target S. The notation (S,Σ_S) explicitly distinguishes the target underlying set and its σ-algebra, and the generated σ-algebra formula quantifies over all B∈Σ_S. This is joint/mutual independence of all finite distinct subcollections, NOT merely pairwise independence, and does not require that the X_n are real-valued. Its prerequisites can be checked against independently screened random-variable, probability-space and independent-σ-algebra meanings after source intake.
